enquiry: Our dairy process includes a relatively clear whey stream before a concentration stage. We want to investigate whether spectroscopy can track protein concentration as the stream changes, with laboratory results used as the reference. The stream can become more turbid under some operating conditions. We need a first measurement concept that handles this change rather than assuming the liquid always remains clear.

assessment.status_reason: A shortlist can be justified: NIR transmission is the source-preferred geometry for clear dairy streams, and ATR probes measure liquids in contact in-line. The protein range, the turbidity range and the required accuracy are not yet known, so the choice between NIR and MIR ATR, and any combination, stays conditional.

recommendations.rationale: Whey is named as a stream for which NIR transmission is preferred, and NIR fiber probes are used for online dairy analysis. NIR bands are broad and overlapping, so a chemometric calibration against the laboratory reference is needed.
recommendations.conditions: Applies while the stream stays transparent enough for transmission; the optical pathlength must be set for the expected protein range, and the calibration is matrix-specific.

citations.quote: Transmission is the preferred method for transparent or semi-transparent liquids, such as skim milk, whey, or permeate.
making it ideal for online applications, including remote measurements via fiber optic probes.
The broad absorption bands observed in this region overlap, suggesting the use of chemometrics for quantitative and qualitative analysis of spectral data.

recommendations.rationale: ATR probes measure liquids and soft samples in contact and are used for in-line process measurement, and the mid-IR sampling layer is very thin, so bulk turbidity of the stream is less likely to dominate the signal. MIR also shows sharp protein bands (amide I and II).
recommendations.conditions: Test when the stream turns turbid or when the NIR transmission signal degrades; ATR needs tight contact and a clean crystal.

citations.quote: ATR fiber probes (Fig.1) enable the analysis of liquids and solid elastic samples

strong absorption in the mid-IR region limits the corresponding spectral method to the analysis of very thin samples (usually less than 50 μm), but it opens up the possibility of using attenuated total reflectance (ATR)
the amide I and II bands, two major absorption peaks of the protein peptide group in the infrared region.

recommendations.rationale: If neither single method covers both the clear and the turbid states, combining the two vibrational methods is a hypothesis to test against the best single method; NIR plus IR combinations have been reported in other applications. Any gain must be demonstrated, not assumed.
recommendations.conditions: Only after the single-method tests, and only if the turbidity change degrades either single method; both probes must view the same small volume of the stream.

solution_options.fusion_note: Fuse the NIR and MIR blocks at low level after block scaling, with one model per method as the baseline, because variables from different methods are not equivalent and must be normalised. Both probes must view the same small volume of the flowing stream, and the two data streams must be normalised to a common time step. Each instrument keeps its own calibration and diagnostics, and the fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs before it is adopted.

assessment.chemometrics_note: Both candidate methods need a chemometric calibration against the laboratory reference: the bands overlap and the calibration is specific to the sample matrix. Build one model per method, keep the reference data with the spectra, and validate on held-out runs or batches.
assessment.realtime_tracking_note: The enquiry is about tracking a changing stream, so the concept should give continuous spectra at the line with results in near real time; fiber probes let the spectrometer sit away from the process point.
assessment.future_direction: Once the informative wavelengths for this stream are known, a compact LED-based sensor could be considered as a later step.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the single-method trials show that NIR transmission or transflection holds its calibration across the turbid states, O1 becomes sufficient; if protein is not separable by either single method, the fused option O3 is the next test. Answers on the protein range and the required accuracy would also change the choice.
proposal.next_step: Agree the sample set, the reference protein method and the go / no-go thresholds with the customer, then run the NIR and MIR ATR single-method trials on the same samples.

assessment.brief_answer: Test NIR transmission (or transflection) first for tracking protein in the whey stream while it stays clear, with your laboratory protein results as the reference. If the turbid states degrade that signal, test MIR ATR on the same samples. A fused NIR+MIR model is only worth testing if neither single method meets your targets. Protein range, turbidity range, required accuracy and installation conditions are still open.

solution_options.fusion_note: Fuse the NIR and MIR blocks at low level after block scaling, with one model per method as the baseline, because variables from different methods are not equivalent and must be normalised. Both probes must view the same small volume of the flowing stream, and the two data streams must be normalised to a common time step. assessment.chemometrics_note: Both candidate methods need a chemometric calibration against the laboratory reference: the bands overlap and the calibration is specific to the sample matrix. assessment.realtime_tracking_note: The enquiry is about tracking a changing stream, so the concept should give continuous spectra at the line with results in near real time; fiber probes let the spectrometer sit away from the process point.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the single-method trials show that NIR transmission or transflection holds its calibration across the turbid states, O1 becomes sufficient; if protein is not separable by either single method, the fused option O3 is the next test. Answers on the protein range and the required accuracy would also change the choice.
proposal.next_step: Agree the sample set, the reference protein method and the go / no-go thresholds with the customer, then run the NIR and MIR ATR single-method trials on the same samples.

assessment.brief_answer: Test NIR transmission (or transflection) first for tracking protein in the whey stream while it stays clear, with your laboratory protein results as the reference. If the turbid states degrade that signal, test MIR ATR on the same samples. A fused NIR+MIR model is only worth testing if neither single method meets your targets. Protein range, turbidity range, required accuracy and installation conditions are still open.
